decisions.reason: As a homepage-promoted extension of the core messaging business in a growing market, it likely meets or is close to aspiration levels and the firm has enough slack to continue it.
Its own dedicated page suggests meaningful managerial commitment and early relevance to document workflows, so a growing, hiring firm would more likely retain it than redeploy resources.
Because it is only briefly mentioned and may face more uncertain demand, its shortfall risk is higher, but its fit with the established communication stack and available slack still favor retention.
This close-in optimization feature probably requires limited additional resources and supports the installed fax business, which makes continuation more likely unless results clearly disappoint.
Security is central to the firm's value proposition, so even with limited website emphasis the product is strategically aligned and likely to be kept while its performance is assessed.

Multi-engine virus scanning is a complementary security add-on with plausible cross-selling value, and under moderate organizational slack the firm would usually keep such a product unless evidence turns clearly negative.
